clue.text: River said to produce a foul, exhalation

indicators.note: said signals that the river's name is spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: the Oder is a river of central Europe on the German-Polish border

explanation.surface: A polluted river is blamed for giving off a nasty smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell given off, especially an unpleasant one, is a foul exhalation.

clue.text: Forest-dweller confused 2 with a nut, perhaps

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters of the combined words are mixed up

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer to 2 down, an instrument

explanation.surface: A forest creature is muddled by a musical instrument and a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' mixes ORGAN (the answer to 2 down) with A and NUT; 'perhaps' links the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape of Borneo and Sumatra lives in rainforest trees.

clue.text: Instrument for decapitating a Welshman?

indicators.note: decapitating cuts off the head, the first letter

parts.note: Morgan is a typically Welsh name

explanation.surface: A grim question about a tool for beheading someone from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with pipes, as in a church.

clue.text: Fresh start is out of order, we learn

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We discover a new beginning is improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting again, or being restored, is beginning afresh.

clue.text: Most important for a girl to play this boy

definitions.text: for a girl to play this boy

explanation.surface: A casting note: the leading boy's role goes to an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime the hero, the 'principal boy', is traditionally played by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief or leading, as in the main thing; and the pantomime hero's role, the principal boy, taken by a woman.

clue.text: Details on which one may win

explanation.surface: Small matters can decide who wins.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxer who wins 'on points' is judged the winner without a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular items or features; and the scoring by which a boxing match can be decided.

clue.text: Immobility sophisticated beginning for play being performed

parts.note: in means fashionable or sophisticated, as in the in crowd
a play begins with Act I
a show being performed is on

explanation.surface: A stiff, unmoving opening to a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing, not moving, is a lack of activity.

clue.text: M.C. changes last two characters round to get equal here

indicators.note: the final two letters of the word swap places, turned the other way about

parts.note: a compere is a master of ceremonies, an MC

explanation.surface: An MC swaps his last two letters to become a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'here' link; 'changes last two characters round' swaps the RE at the end of COMPERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer or companion is someone of equal standing.

clue.text: Poor person in East, not paid for working

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A needy person in the East gets no wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retired lives on a pension rather than wages from a job.

clue.text: University student reversed over one in road — how ghastly

indicators.note: reversed means the two letters are turned the other way round

parts.note: L for learner, a student driver

indicators.note: in places the one inside the road

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A college student crashes and is upside down over someone in the road: horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: UL, the university and student, is reversed to LU; 'over' places it above the rest in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking or sensational, garishly horrible, as in lurid details.

clue.text: A royal male elected by a republic

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy
a gent is a gentleman, a man
a candidate who is elected is in office

explanation.surface: A prince has been voted in to lead a republic, a contradiction in terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American country is a republic, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Grub, perhaps, for Clementine's father

explanation.surface: Asking what food would suit the father of a girl called Clementine.
explanation.walkthrough: In the American folk song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' her father was 'a miner, forty-niner'; a leaf grub is an insect larva that tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: Some insect larvae burrow inside leaves, and the song's father dug for gold in a canyon.

clue.text: Left showing signs of flatulence? That's novel

parts.note: someone who has left is gone
flatulence is wind, so someone suffering it is with the wind

explanation.surface: A rude joke about someone departing while breaking wind, presented as a title.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Margaret Mitchell's 1936 novel of the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's bestselling book about Scarlett O'Hara is a famous example of a long work of fiction.

clue.text: Lags behind republican leader, formally attired

indicators.note: attired means dressed, so the formal clothing is put around the other letter

parts.note: dressing formally for a man means white tie and tails, the tailcoat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from republican

explanation.surface: A Republican Party leader turns up in evening dress yet still falls behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The republican's leader R is dressed in TAILS, the formal tailcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall behind others in a race is to follow at the back, a verb sense.

clue.text: Collection of reminiscences about the old country is upbeat

parts.note: ana is a collection of sayings or anecdotes about a person
c is the abbreviation for circa, about
Rus is the old name for Russia

explanation.surface: A memoir about the homeland is cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: In music and verse, the unstressed notes or syllables before the first strong beat form the upbeat.

clue.text: Turner's device for gaining entry?

parts.note: not the painter Turner but anything turned by a hand to open a door and get in

explanation.surface: It hints at a gadget of the painter J.M.W. Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle on a door is the thing you twist to get into a room.

clue.text: Publican shows cunning in a drinking-spree

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bender is a drinking bout
art can mean cunning or craft, as in artful

explanation.surface: A landlord displays craftiness during a booze-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person serving drinks behind a bar is like a pub landlord.

clue.text: Adman discovered to be unqualified

parts.note: PRO is a public relations officer, someone in promotion like an adman
discovered means found

explanation.surface: An advertising man is revealed to lack qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep and total, without reservation, as in profound ignorance.

clue.text: Clever way to accommodate a male farm employee once

parts.note: neat can mean clever or skilful, as in a neat trick
he is the male pronoun
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A smart way of housing a male labourer on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, so this was a cowherd, an old farm job.

clue.text: Capital of Hungary, a country shaped like a spearhead

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, here from Hungary

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: Budapest, Hungary's capital, in a nation shaped like a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for leaves with a pointed tip and flared base, like a halberd.

clue.text: A number right for one doing the orchestration

parts.note: a score is a number, twenty

explanation.surface: A tidy count is right for the person arranging the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer who arranges music for orchestra writes the full score, so scores it.

clue.text: Outcry about the love of Paris

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for circa, about
in French, the language of Paris, l'amour means the love

explanation.surface: A protest over a romance in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud noisy uproar or protest from many voices.

clue.text: Didn't attempt a question, but satisfied the examiners

explanation.surface: A student skipped a question but got through anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Said no to answering, as in a quiz; and got through a test.

clue.text: Flighty types from the animal park?

definitions.text: Flighty types from the animal park?

parts.words: Flighty types from the animal park?
parts.note: flighty suggests capricious people, but here it means creatures that fly, from a park full of animals that is a paradise for them

explanation.surface: Fickle characters seen leaving a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright-plumed tropical birds of New Guinea, thought of as winged creatures from a happy zoo.

clue.text: Eg, man's attempt to comprehend a form of education

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include, so the attempt contains the education

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A person trying to understand a teaching method.
explanation.definitionFit: A human being walks on two legs, an example of a two-footed creature.

clue.text: The stress present in anarchic tussles

indicators.note: present in signals letters lying within the following words

explanation.surface: Strain shows in chaotic scuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical term for the beat or accent on a syllable in verse.

clue.text: Crush a high-ranking Turk

parts.note: a pash is British schoolgirl slang for a crush or infatuation

explanation.surface: Having a crush on a senior Turkish official.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was given to senior officers and governors in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Not recognized as morally pure

explanation.surface: Someone virtuous goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Not picked out or seen; and without a blemish or stain on one's character.

clue.text: A girl's looked after when affected by inflation

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, with the possessive s
to have looked after someone is to have tended them

explanation.surface: A young woman is cared for as prices rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen or blown up, as a stomach or balloon is by air.

clue.text: He gets up part of the staircase

explanation.surface: Someone climbs out of bed and onto the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting out of bed, an early one; and the vertical board between the treads of steps.
